# Rules: Memory, projects, profile, skills and the Guide

**Covers:** `memory/`, `ltm/`, `brain/`, `learning/`, `profile/`, `personas/`, `skills/`, `guide/`, `workmap/`, `projects/`, `capability/`, `inbox/` (the improvements inbox).

How to use this file: read the contents list, then read only the entries your change touches (each line gives the line number where the full text starts). The rules that apply to every change are in the root `CLAUDE.md`. To add a rule, see "Adding a rule" there.

## Rules

- **The identity spine reaches EVERY prompt seam** (v1.144.0). `profile/`
  renders the user's profile and `personas/voice.py` the assistant's voice;
  both are appended in `daemon/chat_turn.py`, the `/chat/stream` mirror in
  `routes/chat.py`, `agents/runtime.py`, and `agents/threads.py` (the round
  table takes `include=("how",)` only — panelists must stay distinct). A NEW
  surface that talks to the user adds its injection in the same change:
  `tests/test_profile_v1144.py::test_profile_reaches_every_prompt_seam` drives
  all of them end-to-end, and each seam is mutation-proven. "Chat has it,
  agents don't" is the exact bug that wave existed to fix.

- **A rule that lives in one page's JSX is not a rule, and a delete must
  untag what SPAWNS** (v1.220.0, projects-module review). "An archived project
  takes no new tasks" was enforced by hiding the composer on
  `projects/[id]` — the chat module's Tasks surface and `POST
  /projects/{id}/task` never heard of it. Put the refusal in the route (it
  now answers "unarchive the project first", like `/activate`). Same review:
  `DELETE /projects/{id}` untagged sessions/threads/runs but left task
  schedules (payload `project_id`), goal contracts and reflex rules bound —
  each of those CREATES sessions with its project id, so the ghost project
  kept accruing work while `_project_context` found no row and grounded
  nothing, silently. Anything that carries a project id AND spawns must be
  untagged on delete (the response's `untagged` map is the checklist). Also
  found there: a project root skipped the `usable_workspace_root` door that
  `POST /sessions` applies to an explicit `workspace_root` (now
  `_root_problem`, checked at create/patch AND at task time for older rows);
  a knowledge file was staged at `<home>/uploads/<name>` — the exact path
  `/documents/upload` keeps the user's documents at — and clobbered them
  (now a one-off staging dir, removed after extraction); and a deliverable
  stem kept `:*?"<>|` and `..` (`_deliverable_stem`).

- **Task reflections are not knowledge about the user; chat can remember a
  stated preference; the Memory page says what it knows** (v1.279.0, /goal
  memory wave 1). The live ledger: 25 lessons, 23 of them the orchestrator's
  per-run `Worked well for '<task>': <summary>` reflections (weight 1, one
  recording the offline mock's scripted answer), and the top-8 injection under
  "What I've learned about working with you" was six of those. Now
  `LearningEngine.lessons(exclude_sources=)` + `_PROMPT_EXCLUDED_SOURCES =
  ("reflection",)` keep them OUT of `apply_to_prompt` (they still feed
  `dedup`/`distill` and the Lessons tab; `counts_by_source` reports them).
  `remember_preference` had sat in `AUTO_SAFE_TOOLS` since v1.141.0 with NO
  autoselect rule — membership without a rule arms nothing — so "from now on
  keep answers short" reached no memory from chat; a vocabulary rule
  (lasting-instruction shapes: "from now on", "always/never <do>", "I
  prefer", "call me") awards it 7, and `preference_block(armed)` rides the
  Tools seam of BOTH lanes ONLY when the tool is armed (the v1.262.0 rule:
  a brief beside no tool is a lie), lock-step. `memory/overview.py::
  memory_overview(platform)` (never raises; off the loop at
  `GET /memory/overview`) feeds `components/memory/KnowsAboutYou.tsx`, mounted
  at the top of `MemorySurface`; silent when the daemon cannot answer. And
  `_clean_setup` now stores `reasoning` (vocabulary-checked) — the page had
  sent and read it since v1.263.0 while the whitelist dropped it, so the
  level reset on every thread reopen. Pins: `tests/test_memory_knows_you_v1279.py`,
  `dashboard/__tests__/knows-about-you-v1279.test.tsx`; the v1 lesson pin in
  `tests/test_learning.py` moved (a reflection is asserted OUT of the prompt).

- **A preference has a STATUS, and only a confirmed one reaches a prompt;
  the second same correction becomes ONE question** (v1.305.0; ideas from
  agent-personalizer, MIT, Auny LLC — no code taken). `LessonRecord` gained
  nullable `status`/`origin`/`evidence_json`/`signature`/`decided_at`;
  `learning/models.lesson_status` is the ONE place NULL reads as confirmed
  (never rewritten on disk), and `learning/engine.confirmed_clause()` sits
  inside `lessons()` — the single query every reader goes through
  (apply_to_prompt, recall_lessons, fabric, graph, overview, /lessons, cli);
  `improvement/engine.py`'s raw select filters too, and a grep pin lists
  every `.lessons(` caller and raw `select(LessonRecord)` so a new reader is
  caught. `remember_preference` ("from now on …") is unchanged: confirmed,
  origin said, the v1.282.0 receipt. `learning/corrections.py` is pure and
  makes NO model call: `is_correction` needs a correction shape AND a style
  target and refuses task verbs, made things, questions, code, links, a
  correction scoped to one case (`_ONE_OFF`: "for this client", "this time",
  "on my phone"), > 280 chars, > 3 lines (table tests: 42 match / 58
  must-not); `signature` folds
  synonyms and keeps polarity; `similar` = Jaccard ≥ 0.5 + same polarity + a
  shared content token; `proposal_text` builds the sentence from the user's
  OWN words. `learning/preferences.suggest_for_turn` is called by BOTH chat
  lanes (lock-step; only POST /chat and /chat/stream ask, as
  `suggest_preferences=not body.pane_id.strip()` — the sidebar, phone,
  agents AND a Build pane's turn get null: PaneChat renders no line, so a
  pane-minted row would be an unseen question holding an open slot; the
  pane's saved thread still counts as evidence for the main chat): the detector runs
  first, only a correction pays the look-back (`asyncio.to_thread` inside
  `wait_for(2 s)`, wrapped, logs no text) over 30 days of chat + phone lines
  in a DIFFERENT turn (a saved thread matching the body's user lines is this
  conversation — ChatBody carries no thread id); it mints a `proposed` row
  (max 3 open, `mint` serialised) and puts `suggestion` on the done frame /
  POST response ALWAYS (null when none). Declined is FINAL (`_blocked` on the
  signature) until "Ask again" deletes the row; a kept or stated preference
  also blocks. Routes `routes/preferences.py`: `GET /memory/preferences`
  (kept/suggested/never/open_limit/scan.sources), keep {text?} / decline /
  ask-again / PATCH / DELETE (edited text 1–280 chars, promptguard-scanned),
  `POST /memory/preferences/scan {sources}` — consent PER PRESS, the user's
  typed prompts only from each session's OWN file (the history reader's
  subagent fold holds the parent agent's prompts, not the user's; a record
  that starts with markup is the CLI's own — `!` mode stores
  `<bash-stdout>` OUTPUT as a user record — and is skipped), newest 20
  per source, mints only when a Claude Code/Codex line is in the cluster.
  Events preference.suggested {via: chat|scan} / kept / declined. DASHBOARD:
  `lib/preferences.ts` (decoders OUTSIDE api.ts; `decodeSuggestion` is the
  stream hook's whitelist), `components/chat/PreferenceSuggestion.tsx` (the
  quiet line under TurnReceipt: Keep · Edit · Not this; Enter/Escape never
  bubble to the composer; never takes focus), stored on `ChatMessage.
  suggestion` by BOTH lanes; `settledSuggestionsRef` + `applySettled` inside
  `queueSave` so a Keep pressed mid-turn survives that turn's save; a
  keep/decline answered 409/404 (decided on the Memory page / another
  window) re-reads `GET /memory/preferences` and settles to the REAL outcome
  (`settledElsewhere`: kept with the kept words, declined, or `state: "gone"`
  which renders nothing) through the same `onSettle` save — only another
  error (400 flagged, network) shows the sentence;
  `components/memory/PreferenceSections.tsx` (#prefs-kept/-suggested/-never/
  -scan) inside KnowsAboutYou (404 = today's card); the bell maps
  `via == "scan"` only, `quiet` (no badge, no desktop toast). Pins:
  `tests/test_corrections_v1305.py`, `tests/test_preferences_v1305.py`,
  `dashboard/__tests__/preferences-v1305.test.tsx`.
  v1.305.1 (test-only): v1.305.0's Release gate went red on
  `continue-next-v1303` F4 — `findByTestId` found the copy sentence while it
  still read "the next account" (before the light snapshot landed) and
  asserted the NAMED one; the wait is now on the named sentence itself.
  Reproduced locally by delaying the mocked read 150 ms (old shape: CI's exact
  error; new: green).

- **The profile reaches a Build pane ONLY through a switched-on, generated
  block in the CLI's own instructions file — outside text byte-identical,
  a hand edit never overwritten** (v1.306.0; idea from agent-personalizer,
  MIT — no code taken). VERIFIED on this PC, not guessed: Claude Code 2.1.290
  reads `<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude>/CLAUDE.md` as its "User"
  instructions (binary: `case"User":return Ve(we(),"CLAUDE.md")`, `we =
  CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ?? homedir/.claude`; LIVE with a throwaway
  CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and a throwaway USERPROFILE — the session record carried
  the file as an `instructions` attachment even with no login, and the
  `<!-- -->` marker lines were dropped from what the model reads); Codex
  0.157.0 reads `<CODEX_HOME or ~/.codex>/AGENTS.override.md` when it holds
  non-whitespace, else `AGENTS.md` (`codex debug prompt-input` with a
  throwaway CODEX_HOME — no model call; Codex ignores a USERPROFILE override
  for its default home, so `~/.codex` is from the binary/docs). The
  user's real `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` exists and is EMPTY — a file we did not
  create is never deleted. `profile/share.py` (`ProfileShare`, built in
  `build_platform`, `platform.profile_share`): content = `LEAD` +
  `profile.render` + `# Preferences they approved` from
  `confirmed_preferences` (`source == "preference"`, user scope,
  `confirmed_clause()` — feedback/distilled/reflection/project rows never;
  the v1.305.0 raw-select grep pin lists `profile/share.py`), each line
  `promptguard.scan_context` (a flagged preference DROPPED, not
  placeholder'd), `redact.mask`, `scrub_paths`, ≤ 280 per line,
  `MAX_SHARE_CHARS` 4,000 (`omitted` counted), marker words neutralised and `<!--`/`-->` broken up (the CLI drops
  HTML comments, so a typed opener would hide the rest); an
  empty render writes nothing. The REGION is the start marker through the
  end marker plus ONE newline, inserted right after any BOM at the top,
  replaced in place, or cut out — so outside bytes are identical after
  write, rewrite and removal (CRLF/BOM/no-trailing-newline/empty fixtures);
  newline style follows the file; a non-UTF-8 file, damaged markers, or a
  SYMLINKED / HARD-LINKED file are left alone (`os.replace` would turn the
  user's dotfiles link into a plain file — `LINK_ERROR` on the row). State `<IJ home>/profile-share.json` per file: sha256 of the
  normalised region (`hash`), `created`, `backed_up`, `held`, `written_at`.
  DRIFT = region differs from `hash`, or the block/file we wrote is gone →
  never written until `POST /profile/share/{cli}/overwrite {path?}`;
  `POST /profile/share/{cli}/keep {path?}` sets `held` (frozen until
  Overwrite, even if the text matches again). First write to an existing
  file copies it to `<IJ home>/trash/<stamp>/profile-share/<drive>/<path>`
  (once per file); writes are temp + `os.replace`, and the file is read
  AGAIN right before the replace (`_atomic_write(expect=)`, `FileChanged`):
  a save that landed after Jarvis's read wins and the write is abandoned
  (the window left is the re-read-to-replace gap, not the whole write).
  Off removes every tracked block (an edited one copied to trash first) and
  deletes a file WE created that is blank after; a file whose block could
  not come out (locked, a link, damaged markers) stays listed and the row
  still says so with the switch off. HOMES: the default (env var else
  `~/.<cli>`) + every Iron-Proxy CLI account `cli.home` for that provider
  from the CACHED snapshot (never a call); `is_default_home` / same path =
  one file; Iron-Proxy OFF = default only (UNEDITED account blocks taken back);
  Iron-Proxy on but unread (`cached_accounts() is None`) = account files
  left alone. `IronProxyService.add_accounts_listener` fires on
  `set_enabled` and when the snapshot's account-home set changes. TRIGGERS:
  `notify_changed()` after the commit in `ProfileStore.save`,
  `preferences.keep/edit/forget`, `LearningEngine.note_preference`,
  `POST/DELETE /lessons`, the memory graph's lesson delete
  (`POST /memory/graph/node/delete`), plus a boot `poke()` in the lifespan
  — `poke` only arms a `DEBOUNCE_S` (1.5 s) `threading.Timer` named
  `profile-share`, so nothing runs on the loop and boot never waits; at
  shutdown `close()` cancels a pending timer and the lifespan waits (off
  the loop, ≤ 5 s) for a write already running.
  SETTING: `Config.profile_share_claude_code` / `profile_share_codex`,
  persisted by `PUT /profile/share` ONLY (not in `_SETTINGS_KEYS`, the
  `iron_proxy_enabled` reason: a settings write would flip the flag
  without writing or removing anything). Routes (`routes/profile_share.py`,
  all file work in `to_thread`): `GET /profile/share` → `{clis: [{cli,
  label, vendor, available, on, file_name, files: [{path, account, exists,
  last_written, drift, held, created, error}], targets: [{path, account}],
  last_written, drift, accounts_known, chars, omitted}], limit}`; `PUT
  {cli, on}` (404 unknown cli, 409 not installed) → the view after the
  write/removal. DASHBOARD: `components/memory/ProfileShareRow.tsx` at the
  foot of KnowsAboutYou ("Share with Build"; `#profile-share-<cli>`; a CLI
  not found = no switch; 404/failed read = no row), words in
  `lib/profileShare.ts` (`shareSentence` names the files and the vendor
  who sees it; `fileLine` for edited/removed/broken/held/error). Pins:
  `tests/test_profile_share_v1306.py` (real temp homes via
  USERPROFILE/HOME; a teardown check that the REAL files are untouched),
  `dashboard/__tests__/profile-share-v1306.test.tsx`.

- **An MCP memory base WRITES only through tools the user CONFIRMED;
  a refusal is never "unavailable"; a save that landed is never sent twice**
  (v1.408.0, the four open points of v1.406.0, found against the user's REAL
  wiki server hermes-brain — read-only calls, schemas and reply shapes
  recorded in `tests/test_memory_profile_fixes_v1408.py`). `ltm/mcp_roles.py`
  (pure): ROLES search/read/create/append/archive/delete/rename/move, a
  mapping `{tool, args: {param: query|ref|title|content|to|{const}}}`;
  `propose(tools)` is a SUGGESTION (verb order, a note noun, server order);
  `problems()`/`clean()` refuse an unknown tool, a write-like tool as a reader,
  an unfilled REQUIRED param, a comment field (`note`/`reason`/…) as the text,
  a role missing what it needs; `build_args` splits a list-typed fixed value on
  commas. Confirmed roles live in `LTMSourceRecord.roles_json` (additive),
  written ONLY by `PUT /ltm/sources/{name}/roles` (validated against the live
  `tools/list`; GET answers tools + proposed + saved + problems).
  `McpBrainConnector(roles=)`: search/read use a confirmed role else the
  read-only safe pick; `update`/`change` raise `NoteOpUnsupported` with
  `setup_sentence` until confirmed (the v1.406.0 name-word picks for writes
  are gone); `append` uses a confirmed `create` else the LEGACY picker (kept
  for `ltm_append`); `brain/tools.write_note` refuses up front via
  `setup_needed("create")` (kind "setup": nothing sent, nothing queued).
  REPLY SHAPES: a Python MCP SDK server sends a list as `structuredContent
  {"result": [...]}` + one text block PER ITEM (`_result_items`; joined they
  are not JSON and the reply collapsed into one 80-char hit), a read as JSON
  (`note_text` → `content`/`body`/`text`). `write_note` kinds: saved |
  setup | unconfirmed | refused | unreachable; ONLY `unreachable()`
  (transport/timeout/5xx/429/OSError/MCPServerStopped/"did not answer"…,
  walking causes) queues a `BrainPendingWrite`; a raised write is first
  checked with `already_saved` (same-title note already holding the text →
  saved), and Retry checks it BEFORE re-sending. `DELETE /ltm/sources/{name}`
  deregisters the live base (+ closes its client); `/ltm/sources` `bases[].kind`
  is the record's kind (+ `tools_set_up` for mcp). `NotionConnector` on a 400
  reads `GET /databases/{id}` ONCE for the real title column and retries.
  `POST /brain/profiles/{id}/check` (read-only steps reach/search/guide/save)
  and `/test-save` (one real save via `write_note`, never queued). The UI name
  is **Memory profile** (vocabulary canon; both ALLOW entries removed; ids,
  `brain_profile` and `brain_*` unchanged; "brain profile" stays a search
  alias). Dashboard: `components/memory/McpBaseRoles.tsx` (Set up tools),
  Check / Try a test save on each profile. REVIEW (9 defects, each red
  first): `unreachable(exc, sent=)` ignores any word/code that appears in
  what was SENT (a FastMCP refusal echoes the note in `input_value=`, so a
  note saying "connection" was queued forever; codes match whole numbers
  only); `already_saved` needs the WHOLE text at word boundaries (an 80-char
  prefix made a refused correction "saved"); a prose create reply is
  looked up by title; `health()` honours a confirmed search tool;
  `tool_list` reads a FRESH list on a throwaway thread, 20 s bound; an
  empty required value is refused before sending; re-adding a base for
  another server clears `roles_json`; Notion's schema read is remembered
  only once it succeeds; `mcp_roles.writes()` (edit/modify/…/store +
  `readOnlyHint: false` / `destructiveHint`) keeps a writer from reading.
  NOT DONE: Notion's hosted MCP
  (OAuth) cannot be a memory base; the REST connector searches titles in one
  database. Pins: `tests/test_memory_profile_fixes_v1408.py` (14 mutations
  red), `dashboard/__tests__/memory-profile-v1408.test.tsx`.

- **A BRAIN PROFILE names the durable memory base; ONE resolve rule; the
  guide is trusted, every retrieved note is DATA; a save is "saved" only
  when read back; a structural change asks every time** (v1.406.0; the user:
  "Notion as my durable shared brain becomes a selectable system-level
  behaviour, not a giant prompt every agent must remember"; design note
  `docs/BRAIN-PROFILES.md`). `brain/`: `BrainProfileRecord` +
  `BrainPendingWrite` (late models, `core.db._LATE_MODEL_MODULES`);
  `profiles.resolve(platform, project_id)` is THE rule (`Project.brain_profile`
  "" = follow `Config.brain_profile`, "off" = none, else an id; a stale id =
  none; never raises). The app choice is schema row `brain_profile` (tier
  ask — where Jarvis SAVES is a privacy call), controlled in its own Settings
  section (`CONTROLLED_IN_SECTION`); a project's rides `PATCH /projects/{id}`
  (an unknown id 400s). `brain/turn.build_turn_bounded` (off the loop, 8 s,
  copies the context so Local only reaches its thread) builds ONE block for
  BOTH chat lanes (`chat_turn.brain_turn`, gathered BESIDE
  `_gather_grounding` and joined right BEFORE `before_attachments()` — the
  `_Grounding` order pin is untouched) AND the agent runtime (after the
  identity spine; not for a review-only helper or `skip_memory`): the rules,
  the OPERATING GUIDE (a note in the primary, cached 10 min, promptguard-
  scanned, followed as instructions), the profile's skills
  (`guarded_instructions`), and the primary searched with the turn's question
  — every hit scanned AND `wrap_untrusted`-fenced. Tools `brain_search` /
  `brain_read` (READONLY, `returns_untrusted_content`), `brain_save`,
  `brain_change` resolve the profile from `ctx.project_id`, else the
  session row's project (the runtime's ToolContext carries none), registered
  through `_LazyPlatform`, armed by `chat_turn.brain_armed` after every fill
  pass (both lanes) and by the runtime only while a profile is USABLE (not
  missing, not a remote base under Local only); `brain_save`/`brain_change`
  are in `LOW_TRUST_DENY`. `brain_save`: about="code" refused while
  `repo_routing` (the repo's own AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/docs), `save_to` never =
  refused, ask = `spend_check` card; looks the note up by slugged title and
  `update`s it (`LTMConnector.update/read/change` are optional, raise
  `NoteOpUnsupported`), else appends; READS BACK (`_verify`): found = saved,
  cannot read = "saved, not confirmed", read but missing = NOT saved and NOT
  queued (it may have landed); a write that raised is a `BrainPendingWrite`
  ("unsaved change", `GET /brain/pending`, Retry through the SAME
  `write_note`, Discard). `brain_change` (archive/delete/rename/move):
  `SpendCheck(ask=True, once_only=True, reason="memory")` EVERY call, every
  posture; a folder base MOVES the note into its `.trash` (hidden from
  search), never unlinks; `_note_path` refuses anything resolving outside the
  folder. Receipt `brain` (null with no profile) is the LAST key of the POST
  answer and the done frame, folded OUTSIDE the `if ran:` gate (an unsaved
  save must be said). Dashboard: `lib/brainProfiles.ts`,
  `components/settings/BrainProfiles.tsx`, `project/ProjectBrainSelect.tsx`,
  `chat/ChatBrainLine.tsx`, `memory/BrainUnsaved.tsx`, TurnReceipt
  `turn-brain` (collapsed, unsaved first in warn) / `turn-brain-detail`;
  `lib/onceReason` "memory" (its own card line, never Enter-allowed). The
  vocabulary canon retires "brain": sentences say "memory base"; "Brain
  profile" is allowed ONLY as the feature's name (both vocabulary scans hold
  one ALLOW entry). Also: `ltm_search` output is now fenced
  (`returns_untrusted_content`). Off is byte-identical — the harness-off
  golden moved only by the new `brain` key. Pins:
  `tests/test_brain_profiles_v1406.py`, `tests/test_brain_profiles_review_v1406.py`,
  `dashboard/__tests__/brain-*-v1406.test.tsx`. REVIEW (11 defects, each red
  first): a run that CANNOT ask (a delegated child, an unattributed API run)
  now REFUSES a call whose own `spend_check` says ask — it used to run an
  allow-tier tool uncarded (generic: a git push in a delegated child too); a
  dotted title ("Plan v1.2") reached another note (`with_suffix`) — ".md" is
  APPENDED; a `\\host` ref is refused by spelling before any `exists()` /
  `resolve()` (the v1.379.0 SMB lesson); the MCP pick ranks append before
  update and note words first, never set/write/overwrite; the bounded build's
  fallback uses a CACHED guide only; Notion reads page through its cursor and
  writes in 2,000-char pieces; a base's own error text is scanned before it
  reaches the prompt; the block never offers a writer the turn lacks
  (`writers=` from both lanes + the runtime, `BrainTurn.without_tools()` for
  text-only / coding-session turns); Undo of an update snapshots the REAL
  path and exact bytes; an unsaved receipt entry carries `kept` (sent to the
  Memory page only when it is listed there). A READ-ONLY agent type (nothing
  in `runtime._BRAIN_WRITER_ROLES` on its roster — Reviewer, the Guide) gets
  the readers only. OPEN: an MCP base's read/update/change tools are
  picked by name words; Retry can add twice when an earlier attempt landed
  and then raised; `DELETE /ltm/sources/{name}` still does not
  deregister the live base and `/ltm/sources` reports a custom base's kind as
  its name (older than this change).

- **A project KNOWS its coding sessions: resolved by FOLDER at read time,

  `harness/sessions.checkout_of`, a folderless session none) resolved by

  may_recall_local_only_chats()` (the fabric recall's rule, read from the

  BYTE-IDENTICAL with no chats/coding sessions (pinned in both lanes and the

  set (two-argument test doubles). The look-back is UNCHANGED:
  coding sessions stay out of the "other conversations" scan (the v1.367.0
  pin), so a session's own stored copy — whose first line a Compact can drop

  keeps `suggestion` (a LINE_KEY both sides); `GET /build/sessions/{id}`

- **A skill works in a coding session the way the harness it came from runs

  `~/.config/opencode/skill(s)`, `~/.pi/agent/skills`. NOT read: Grok's

  still is). A session FOLDER's own skills (`project_skills`): `.claude/
  skills` (one level), `.agents/skills`, `.grok/skills`, `.opencode/
  skill(s)`, `.pi/skills` from the folder up to the first folder holding
  `.git` (none: the folder alone; never the home), nearest first; source
  `project` = SCANNED; the registry wins a name (Claude Code: personal
  before project). FRONTMATTER (`loader.Skill`): `when_to_use`/`when-to-use`,
  `model_invocable` (`disable-model-invocation`, and Codex's
  `agents/openai.yaml` `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false`),
  `user_invocable`, `argument_names`, `argument_hint` (a YAML list joined
  like JavaScript's String), `allowed_tools` (READ, NEVER OBEYED). LISTING
  (`native.listing`, `HarnessTurn.skill_listing`, built in
  `chat_turn._build_harness` off the loop when `skill_load` is in the gate,
  after the rendered harness and before the date, NOT in the fingerprint):

  4 chars, 1,536 a description, shortened evenly, names only last;
  model-invocable only; harness-layer folder skills stay in the tree's own
  list. INVOCATION (`native.invocation_text` — ONE function for
  `skill_load` and both chat lanes' `/name`): `Base directory for this

  → `<plugin>:<skill>`, refuses a non-model-invocable skill in words;

  scratch CODEX_HOME confirmed `.agents/skills` from the folder up to the

- **THE WORK RECORD: what Iron Jarvis did, in which folder, built only from
  its own records; a chat is told of a piece of work only after its SOURCE
  was asked again** (v1.491.0; vision plan leap 3, Phase 1,
  `docs/VISION-PLAN-2026-11-14.md`; the owner: "a memory that compounds …
  full steam"; a builder + an independent reviewer who found 4 high and 7
  medium defects, each a test now).
  - **What it is.** `src/iron_jarvis/workmap/`: `models.WorkEntry` (table
    `workentry`, a late model) = one row per piece of work that has a FOLDER:
    kind `chat` | `code` (Chat › Code) | `tool_code` (Build › Code) | `run`;
    title, folder + `folder_key`, files (newest first, ≤ 40, from a reply's
    `documents` and the undo journal), outcome, `local_only`, `keep_home`
    (Pi / OpenCode), `archived`, a run's summary line. A DERIVED index: no
    model call, no file on disk opened, deleting it loses nothing.
  - **Sources (`collect.py`).** A conversation is work only once Jarvis has
    REPLIED in it (the page saves a new chat's question before its first turn
    names its thread: it must never be listed to itself). Never a phone
    thread (`owner == "daemon"`), a hosted helper (`handed_from`), a hosted
    session whose tool never answered, a helper / mission-member run
    (filtered IN the SQL, so they never use up the listing bound), a
    delegated child (`AgentRun.parent_id`), or a run in its own scratch
    folder with no project. A STAMP decides what is rebuilt; it holds the
    title (a coding session's rename does not move `updated_at`) and the
    journal's row + undone counts (`journal_counts`, one grouped read).
  - **Keeping it (`index.WorkMap`, `work_map(engine, home)` one per
    engine).** `refresh()` is throttled (20 s), never waits for another
    refresh, builds ≤ 60 rows inline and hands the rest to ONE daemon thread
    (`_build_rest`: one scan, 25-row transactions). No loop wakes for it: it
    runs right before a read. A source that cannot be listed leaves its rows
    alone; a row past a listing's bound is removed only when
    `collect.source_exists` says its source is gone; one row that cannot be
    built or stored is skipped (`_skip`) until its source changes. A hosted
    read that fails RAISES (never "no rows"). `files_json` is ASCII JSON and
    every text goes through `storable_text`.
  - **What a chat is told (`block.work_block`, hop `work` in
    `_gather_grounding`, joined in `_Grounding.query()` right after the
    project's query part).** "In this folder" (newest six, repeats folded)
    for the turn's `workspace_dir`, else the project's root; inside a project
    that part is left to the project's own recent activity. "In other
    folders, matching this message" via `WorkMap.matching`. BEFORE anything
    is said, `collect.live_state` asks each row's source by id: gone → not
    said; Local only / archived read from the source, not the row. Sources
    unreadable → "". Local only and `keep_home` rows only for a turn that
    `egress.may_recall_local_only_chats`. Archived never. Every line through
    promptguard. "" when nothing is on record (both lanes byte-identical,
    pinned against the hop switched off).
  - **THE MATCHING RULE IS STRICT ON PURPOSE** (the first cut pulled other
    clients into "What are the 2025 tax brackets?"): `keys.words` = lower-case
    words of 4+ letters that are not stop words, bare numbers or file
    endings; a row matches with TWO such words of which one belongs to few
    folders (`≤ max(1, folders // 10)`), or with ONE word written as a NAME
    in the message (`keys.named_words`: capitalised, not starting its
    sentence) that is the name of exactly one folder; more than
    `QUERY_WORDS_MAX` (30) words is a paste and matches nothing. Looks at the
    newest `LIGHT_MAX` (3,000) rows. Change it only with rows added BOTH ways
    to the two parametrized tables in the test file.
  - **Paths are compared as TEXT** (`keys.folder_key`, `inside`,
    `home_folder`: a `<repo>.ij-worktrees/<name>` copy belongs to `<repo>`);
    nothing stats or resolves (pinned with the disk calls patched to raise).
  - **Routes** (`routes/work_map.py`): `GET /work-record/folders`
    (`folders_total`, `building`; 503, never an empty list, when the record
    cannot be read) and `GET /work-record/entries?folder=` (exactly that
    folder). NOT under `/memory/`: `GET /memory/{layer}/{key}` answers any
    two-part path there. Dashboard: `components/memory/WorkByFolder.tsx` +
    `lib/workRecord.ts` (no `ApiError` import: failures read through
    `failureOf`), mounted under KnowsAboutYou.
  - **OPEN:** recaps, clients, recall in agent runs and a lookup tool are
    Phases 2-4; Build › Code files are not read; `matching` is lexical and
    English; a chat with a folder AND a project lists the folder part only
    through the project's block; no setting turns the block off; a worktree
    copy's subfolder maps to the whole repository; not driven with a real
    model or in the packaged app.
  - **Pins:** `tests/test_work_record_v1491.py` (55; 31 mutations, all red),
    `dashboard/__tests__/work-by-folder-v1491.test.tsx`.

- **A RECAP of finished work is written by the conversation's own model and
  kept only where the conversation's record supports it; it is told only in
  ITS OWN folder; a folder can be FORGOTTEN** (v1.494.0, BUILT AS v1.492.0:
  another session released v1.493.0 meanwhile, so the code comments and the
  test files keep the tag v1.492.0 / v1492; vision plan leap 3,
  Phase 2; the owner pressed "Memory: recaps"; a builder + TWO independent
  reviews: the first found 3 high and 20 smaller defects, the second 7 more
  in the fixes; each is a test now).
  - **What it is.** `workmap/recap.py` + table `workrecap` (`WorkRecap`, its
    OWN table: `WorkEntry` rows are rebuilt whole with `db.merge`, which would
    wipe recap columns). For a CHAT or a Chat › Code session (never a run,
    which has its own summary line, never Build › Code) quiet for `IDLE_S`
    (600 s): ONE `router.complete(pin=True, tools=[])` on the newest reply's
    own served provider and model (`served_by`; never another agent's line,
    `panelWho`), on the conversation's account (`_pin`: `choice.pin_for` for a
    chat, `turn_account` for a coding session, only when the setup names an
    account), inside `egress.local_only_scope(local_only)`, bounded
    `RECAP_TIMEOUT_S` 90, billed to the conversation (`library._bill`; a
    billing failure never loses the recap).
  - **THE CHECK (`recap.check`, pure).** A line is kept only when it starts
    `DONE:` / `DECIDED:` / `OPEN:` (shown as Done / Decided / Open), is at
    most `RECAP_LINE_CHARS`, and EVERYTHING CHECKABLE in it is on record
    (the conversation as the model was
    SHOWN it, or the work entry's own file list):
    - every NUMBER, any size (`_NUMBER_RX` + `_number_key`: "1,234.50" =
      "1234.5"; "12,50", "9,99,999" and "1.491.0" are only themselves; a
      leading dot after a space or sign is a decimal, after a letter
      ("no.4471") punctuation). A SCALE is part of the number: a short one
      only when glued on ("25k", "15B"; "2 K-1 forms" is two K-1s), a word
      after a space or hyphen (thousand, million, mil, grand, lakh…, plurals
      too). A count the conversation wrote as a WORD (one..twelve) is on
      record as its digit (`counts_in_words`), never the other way round. A
      number inside a KNOWN file's name is on record only there
      (`_without_known_files`): it vouches for no other use in the line. The
      first cut skipped numbers under three digits ("15%", "$95", "April 15")
      and any number written right after a dot or comma.
    - every quoted span in ANY marks, matched or not (`_QUOTE_RXS`: straight,
      curly, low, guillemets, corner brackets, backticks; a single quote only
      at a word's start and end; a full stop inside the marks is ignored),
      word for word in the conversation.
    - every file name (`_FILE_RX`: an ending of 1 to 10 characters, dot-files;
      "e.g" / "U.S" are abbreviations), every token written with a slash (a
      path, a folder; "a/r", "n/a", "and/or" are words: `_SHORT_SLASH_RX`),
      every e-mail address: each as a WHOLE token (`_tokens`, `_file_names`),
      never a part of a real one ("march.xlsx" is not "recon_march.xlsx",
      "b@x.com" is not "bob@x.com", "C:\\Clients\\Hart" is not
      "…\\Hartleys"). `_TOKEN_TRIM` takes marks, brackets, `<>`, `*` and
      backticks off both sides.
    - unchanged by `detections.redact.mask`; not flagged by promptguard.
    At most `MAX_RECAP_LINES` 8. `NONE` or no surviving line = no recap. The
    conversation text is clipped at a SPACE (`_clip_words`), so half a number
    is never "on record". `compaction.verify` is NOT used (it accepts a path
    by its last part and reads only straight double quotes). NOT checked
    (said in the Handbook): a name, a figure in words, a dropped "not",
    numbers each on record but put together anew. Strict on purpose: a true
    line is sometimes dropped. The regexes are linear (child-process pins).
  - **NEVER / LATER.** Written down as a `none` row (not looked at again
    until the conversation changes): too short (`MIN_LINES` 4), a reply at low
    trust (its own `trust` or a delivered agent run's `runResult.trust`;
    checked BEFORE the same-lines re-stamp, so a reply marked low trust
    later takes a kept recap away), no
    model on record, the demo model (asked OR answering), Local only with a
    model `egress.stays_on_this_network` refuses, a model that BILLS PER USE
    (`_bills_per_use` → `providers/billing.billing_kind`, unsure = pay:
    `WHY_PAY`), nothing supported. `SETUP_REASONS` (Local only, pay) come
    from a setting, so they are never re-stamped: the same lines are looked at
    again when the conversation's row changes. WAITS with nothing written: a
    reply running in that conversation OR an unfinished agent run started
    from it (`_running_threads`: ACTIVE/QUEUED `Session.options_json
    ["chat_thread_id"]`), the conversation changed again,
    `library.account_refusal`, the provider not available (`never_probe`), a
    recap asked within `REWRITE_GAP_S` (1 h), Emergency stop,
    `RECAPS_PER_DAY` 30, the setting off. A conversation that had to wait is
    left alone for `WAIT_RETRY_S` (`_WAITING`, in memory, skipped BEFORE the
    `EXAMINE_MAX` count; one asked within the hour for what is left of it)
    so it never blocks the ones behind it. A FAILED call
    is tried `MAX_TRIES` 2 times in all for the SAME lines (`covers`), then
    left.
  - **RIGHT BEFORE THE CALL (`_still_ready`).** The conversation is asked
    again: gone, changed, archived or running = nothing sent; switched to
    Local only since the pick = sent only inside the scope to a model on this
    network, else a `none` row and nothing sent. The call runs as a task made
    INSIDE the scopes and is polled every second: Emergency stop or the
    switch going off CANCELS it (`WAIT_STOPPED`).
  - **NOTHING PAID FOR IS ASKED TWICE.** Every store goes through `_keep`
    (never raises; a row that cannot be written leaves the conversation alone
    for `REWRITE_GAP_S`); `write_one` never raises except for a cancel.
    `pass_once` DOES raise when the record itself cannot be read: the loop
    reports that as its health row.
  - **NEVER A BURST.** `<home>/work-recaps.json` holds `since` (written the
    first time a pass runs; only work whose `updated_at` is later, and within
    `LOOK_BACK_DAYS` 14, is recapped), `calls` (today's call times:
    `note_call` / `calls_today`, so a restart does not forget the daily
    limit) and `off` (`note_off` when a pass sees the switch off; `back_on`
    then moves `since` to NOW and answers False when that could not be
    written: the pass then recaps nothing). `_read_marker`: a MISSING file
    or rubbish = `{}` (start from now), a file that cannot be READ just now
    = None, which is never answered by writing a new marker (it moved
    `since` to now and dropped the day's calls). A call stamped up to a day
    in the future still counts (the clock was set back). No marker that
    can be kept = nothing is recapped. One model call per pass (`pass_once`), a pass every
    `PASS_EVERY_S` 180 (`bg_tasks["work_recaps"]`, `_tick("work_recaps")`,
    `lib/loopWords` row; off pops the row). A pass with nothing to do reads
    only light columns of the candidates' threads (never `messages_json`).
  - **A FAILED BACKGROUND CALL RINGS NOTHING.** `providers/background_call.
    background(name)` (a ContextVar around ONE call); `ModelRouter.
    _publish_provider_event` adds `background: name` to that call's
    `provider.failed` (label stays last) and `comm/notifier.on_event` returns
    None for it. The ledger and the breaker still record it. A NEW background
    nicety that calls a model uses the same scope.
  - **WHAT A CHAT IS TOLD.** `collect.live_state` also answers a
    conversation's `updated` stamp; `block._with_recaps` attaches a recap
    ONLY to rows in EXACTLY the turn's folder (`folder_key(home_folder(row))
    == own`; a session's own copy counts as its folder) and only when
    `recap.current_for(recap, live updated)`. NEVER to an "in other folders"
    row (the first review: Hartleys' figures told to a chat in Smith's
    folder through a like-worded request) and NEVER to work in a folder
    UNDER the turn's (the second review: a chat opened on `…\\Clients` was
    told every client's recap; `for_folder` lists subfolders). Lines are indented under the work's own
    line (`recap_lines`: whole lines, `RECAP_CHARS` 520, each through the
    scanner again); `RECAP_NOTE` is added ONCE and only when a recap is
    shown, so a block with no recap is byte-identical to v1.491.0's.
    `BLOCK_CHARS` 3600. `WorkMap.matching` does not read recaps.
  - **FORGET A FOLDER.** Table `workforgotten`; `WorkMap.forget(folder)`
    takes the folder AS SPELLED (rows are keyed that way; mapping it through
    `keys.home_folder` forgot the wrong folder), deletes the entries in and
    under it and in a coding session's own copies of it
    (`<folder>.ij-worktrees/…`, `index.covered`) with their recaps, and keeps
    them out (`_write` treats a covered candidate as not work); the top of a
    drive, the top of a share or server and anything that is not a whole
    location ("books", "..") is refused (`_FORGETTABLE`); `remember` deletes the row, clears `_skip` and the
    throttle. `entries(folder)` reads exactly the folder asked for
    (`for_folder(as_spelled=True)`). Routes `POST /work-record/forget|
    remember {folder}`; `GET /work-record/folders` adds `forgotten`; entries
    carry `recap {lines, written_at, current}`. `_store` keeps nothing for a
    work entry that left the record meanwhile. Deleted work takes its recap
    with it (`_refresh`).
  - **Setting** `work_recaps` (Memory & you, allow, default ON). A new
    schema row means regenerating `capability_search/phrasings.py`; the
    `claude` CLI was at its weekly limit and the local server refused for want
    of a key, so the one entry's eight phrases were written by a Haiku
    subagent given only the generator's prompt.
  - **OPEN:** runs and Build › Code get no recap; inside a Project the "in
    this folder" list is the project's own (titles only, no recap), and a
    Project's recent activity does not read `workforgotten`; a failed recap
    call can strike the provider's breaker; a recap of ordinary (not Local
    only) work done on a local model is told to a later cloud chat in that
    folder, as its title already was; work done under Emergency stop, a
    daily limit or an account wait is recapped afterwards, one call a pass;
    a setting-made "never" (Local only, pay per use) is looked at again
    only when the conversation's row changes; not driven in the packaged
    app.
  - **Pins:** `tests/test_work_recaps_v1492.py`,
    `tests/test_work_recaps_review_v1492.py` (the first reviewer's 25 proofs
    + the fixes it described), `tests/test_work_recaps_review2_v1492.py`
    (the second reviewer's), `dashboard/__tests__/work-recaps-v1492.test.tsx`
    (97 mutations);
    moved on purpose: `work-by-folder-v1491` (a folder row has two buttons;
    `forgotten` in the decoded folders).

- **THE IMPROVEMENTS INBOX: one read over every waiting suggestion; it
  decides NOTHING itself** (v1.496.0, BUILT AS v1.495.0: another session
  released v1.495.0 meanwhile, so the code comments and the two test files
  keep the tag v1.495.0 / v1495; vision plan leap 5, Phase 1,
  `docs/VISION-PLAN-2026-11-14.md`; the owner: "yes proceed"; a builder + an
  independent reviewer who found 13 defects, each a test now).
  - **What it is.** `GET /improvements` (`daemon/routes/improvements.py`, a
    sync `def`) → `inbox/collect.collect(d)` → `{items, groups: [{kind,
    label, count, shown}], total, unreadable: [{kind, label}]}`. Ten kinds,
    in `collect.KINDS` order: `preference` (`LessonRecord` status proposed),
    `skill` (`SkillProposalRecord` pending), `coach` and `habit`
    (`CoachProposalRecord` pending; kind `team_note` is a habit), `lesson`
    and `session_edit` (`HarnessLibraryRecord` proposed; `layer_edit` is a
    session edit), `memory` (`MemoryProposalRecord` pending), `tool`
    (`CapabilityProposalRecord` pending), `wants` (`ProposalRecord`
    pending), `unasked` (a goal's offers to use a tool without asking, from
    `routes/goals`' own `exact_offers` / `grant_offers`). No model call,
    nothing written.
  - **THE RULE: no decision code.** Every item carries `accept` / `decline`
    = `{label, method: "POST", path, body, note, confirm, blocked}` naming the
    suggestion's OWN route. A source-level pin refuses `.accept(`,
    `.approve(`, `db.add(` … in `inbox/collect.py` and holds the route
    prefixes to the seven suggestion routes. A NEW kind of suggestion adds a
    builder + a source function there and a pattern in the dashboard's
    `DECISION_PATHS`; it never adds a route.
  - **EVERY KIND IS READ WITH THE INBOX'S OWN QUERY, WHICH RAISES**
    (`collect._pending(engine, model, *where)`: a count + the newest
    `PER_KIND` 30 rows, `created_at DESC, rowid DESC`). Three stores' own
    `list` swallow a failure and answer `[]` (`memory/proposals`,
    `capability/store`, `goals/store`, and `routes/goals._ask_rows`), so the
    first cut read a locked database as "nothing waiting". `routes/goals.
    ask_rows_strict` is `_ask_rows` without the catch. A failed source names
    every kind it answers for in `unreadable`; `_built` skips ONE row that
    cannot be shown (the count still includes it). A build with no such
    service (`platform.coach` None) lists nothing for it and is not
    "unreadable".
  - **WHAT AN ACCEPT WILL DO IS READ FROM THE RECORD.** A memory tidy-up is
    built from `routes/memory_review.suggestion_view(store, p)` (lifted to
    module level; the card's own view): `collect.memory_effect` (the Python
    twin of MemoryReview.tsx `effectOf`) says which notes are deleted or
    replaced, by name; the model's `suggested_action` is evidence ("The
    suggestion says: …"), never the note. `blocked` (the reason, before the
    press): a memory base that is not connected (`base_note`), a tool Iron
    Jarvis cannot add (`can_apply` / the floor), "Approve and run" under
    Emergency stop (`STOPPED_BLOCK`; the route answers 403, which
    `lib/api.ts` reads as "not signed in") and a maintainer task with
    Self-development off (`SELF_DEV_BLOCK`). A habit's note follows
    `config.team_notes` (`HABIT_OFF_NOTE`).
  - `confirm: true` for an accept that acts at once (`memory`, `tool`,
    `wants`) and for the `wants` Reject (final; two presses on Autonomy too).
    `unasked` has NO accept/decline (a permission is answered on Autonomy);
    `extra {goal_id, tool, args_hash}` lets the page hide one this browser
    answered "Not now". Offers are looked for only on goals that have EVER
    asked (`_goals_with_asks`: one query over Session origins `goal:%` with
    an `approval.requested` event, at most `GOALS_MAX` 60; more → the kind is
    named in `unreadable` as incomplete, via `Read.partial`), and a goal's
    grants are read once (`_GrantsOnce`).
  - **Dashboard.** `/improvements` (`app/improvements/page.tsx`, title
    "Improvements" = the `NON_RAIL_ENTRIES` label; `GROUP_OF` knowledge; not
    a sidebar row). `lib/improvements.ts`: `decodeInbox` (whitelist),
    `isDecisionPath` (`DECISION_PATHS`: the seven routes, ONE id of
    `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` and its own verbs: a browser reads a backslash as a
    slash and resolves dot segments, so "anything but a slash" let
    `/proposals/x\..\..\reviews\s1/approve` through), home links in-app only
    (no `//`, backslash or control character), `answerNote` (the accept
    route's own `note`), `stillWaiting` + `groupsToShow` (`more` = count
    minus the items this page could read). `components/improvements/
    ImprovementsInbox.tsx`: reads on mount, when the window is looked at
    again (not hidden, not within `FOCUS_REREAD_MS`), after an answer, after
    a 404/409 refusal (the suggestion changed elsewhere: the refusal goes to
    the page note) and on `IMPROVEMENT_EVENT_TYPES` (debounced); never on a
    clock; a sequence guard drops a late older read; `gone` hides an answered
    item at once and is reset by every read. `PressButton`: two presses for
    `confirm`, and a second press within `SECOND_PRESS_AFTER_MS` (400) of the
    first does not count (a double click). `lib/goalOffers.ts` holds the "Not
    now" key the Autonomy page and this page share.
  - **THE PACKAGE SHADOWS ITS MODULE** (the v1.254.0 trap, again):
    `inbox/__init__` re-exports the function `collect`, so tests reach the
    module with `importlib.import_module("iron_jarvis.inbox.collect")`.
  - **OPEN:** no count in the bell or on the home line (Phase 2's morning
    line); action approvals, reviews and skill tidy-up are not listed; an
    offer answered "Not now" in another browser profile is still listed; a
    refine of a skill, a coach change and a session edit are one press, as on
    their own screens; the shared `ConfirmButton` elsewhere still takes a
    double click as two presses; not driven in the packaged app.
  - **Pins:** `tests/test_improvements_inbox_v1495.py`,
    `dashboard/__tests__/improvements-inbox-v1495.test.tsx`.

- `guide/` — THE IRON JARVIS GUIDE (v1.224.0; v1.223.0 shipped it as a chat
  persona, which the user rejected — it belongs in the AGENTS module). A
  built-in agent, `AgentType.GUIDE` in `agents/types.py`, in the roster
  beside the other builtins. BASE KNOWLEDGE: `agents/runtime` injects
  `guide.base_knowledge` (the Handbook's overview + this install's live
  version facts) into every Guide session. TOOLS (`guide/tools.py`, all
  read-only, all `allow`): `guide_search`/`guide_read` over `corpus.py` — the
  bundled docs (`BUNDLED_DOCS`, shipped into `_MEIPASS/ijdocs` by the .spec,
  which IMPORTS that list so the bundle cannot drift) plus live catalogs from
  the running daemon (version, providers, tools, skills, personas, agent
  types, every API route with its docstring) — and `app_search`/`app_status`
  over the user's OWN things in this install (projects, workflows,
  schedules, reflex rules, goals, skills, agents, threads, sessions, memory
  bases, custom tools), each hit with the dashboard path that opens it, and
  an unreadable store NAMED rather than reported empty. Retrieval is BM25 +
  phrase bonus + a user-facing doc prior — deterministic, no embedder. THE
  ROUND TABLE HAS NO TOOLS (`PANEL_NO_TOOLS`), so for a Talk with the Guide
  `threads._speak_local` runs the retrieval + app_search itself and appends
  the material AFTER the no-tools rule (`_guide_material`); Give-work and a
  `guide` session get the real tools. `routes/guide.py` is the inspection
  surface (`/guide/status|search|ground`); the Help page's "Ask the Guide"
  box lands in `/agents?talk=guide&ask=…`. Chat can also arm
  `guide_search`/`app_search`/`app_status` (autoselect, narrow vocabulary).
  The Guide knows what the DOCS know: when a surface ships, the Handbook is
  part of the change set, or the Guide answers "not covered" about a feature
  that exists (the doctor check `guide_docs` catches a missing FILE, not a
  stale one).

- `profile/` — the user profile (ONE row): `models` (record), `store`
  (read-never-writes, partial save), `presets` (vocabularies; unknown key =
  free text), `language` (pure script-level leakage detector), `block`
  (the one renderer, bounded + never raises). `personas/builtins.py` holds the
  built-in catalog (importable — `app.py` still exposes it as `d._PERSONAS`).

- `skills/` — recursive discovery incl. `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.claude/plugins`,
  `~/.codex/skills` (`framework.py::external_skill_roots`); registry
  repopulates IN PLACE; skills inject into prompts (provider-agnostic), the
  agent-facing tools are just search/load. `workflows/` — store + engine
  (note: `POST /workflows/run` spawns the run in the background and returns the
  record immediately; it does NOT block until steps finish). `ltm/`,
  `memory/`, `comm/`, `computeruse/`, `sandbox/`, `scheduling/`.
